data.title: Railway Track Diverters
data.statement:
In an automated freight rail yard, trains are routed through a network of [[N]] track diverter switches (numbered {{1}} to [[N]]).

Each switch has a current orientation: {{L}} (Left) or {{R}} (Right).

When a train enters a switch:
1. It follows the track indicated by the switch's current orientation ([[leftTarget]] if {{L}}, [[rightTarget]] if {{R}}).
2. Immediately after the train passes, the switch automatically toggles its state ({{L}} flips to {{R}}, and {{R}} flips to {{L}}).

A target can either be:
- Another switch number (between {{1}} and [[N]])
- A terminal depot name (an alphanumeric label representing the journey's end)

Every train enters the yard at switch {{1}} and travels through switches until reaching a terminal depot.
Trains are dispatched sequentially: each train completely finishes its run and updates all traversed switches before the next train is released.

Given the layout and initial states of all switches, find the final depot reached by each of the [[T]] dispatched trains.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

In an automated freight rail yard, trains are routed through a network of N track diverter switches (numbered 1 to N).

Each switch has a current orientation: L (Left) or R (Right).

When a train enters a switch:
1. It follows the track indicated by the switch's current orientation (leftTarget if L, rightTarget if R).
2. Immediately after the train passes, the switch automatically toggles its state (L flips to R, and R flips to L).

A target can either be:
- Another switch number (between 1 and N)
- A terminal depot name (an alphanumeric label representing the journey's end)

Every train enters the yard at switch 1 and travels through switches until reaching a terminal depot.
Trains are dispatched sequentially: each train completely finishes its run and updates all traversed switches before the next train is released.

Given the layout and initial states of all switches, find the final depot reached by each of the T dispatched trains.
Input
Line 1: An integer N representing the number of switches.
Line 2: An integer T representing the number of trains to dispatch.
Next N lines: An integer id, a character initialState (L or R), and two strings leftTarget and rightTarget separated by spaces.
Output
T lines: The name of the terminal depot reached by each train in dispatch order.
Constraints
1 ≤ N ≤ 50
1 ≤ T ≤ 100
The track network contains no loops.
Example
Input
3
3
1 L 2 3
2 L E1 E2
3 L E3 E4
Output
E1
E3
E2
